hints: Focus on what isomer means for alcohols, same molecular formula but different arrangement of atoms.
Count the total carbon atoms in each name, remembering that methyl branches add extra carbons to the parent chain.
Look for the pair where both alcohols have four carbons in total, so both share the formula C4H10O but with different skeletons.
walkthrough:
**Recall what isomers need**

Isomers must have exactly the same molecular formula but a different structural arrangement. For alcohols, that means the same total number of C, H and O atoms.

Rule:
$$\text{same molecular formula} + \text{different structure} = \text{isomers}$$

**Count carbons in each alcohol**

The parent name gives the main chain, and any methyl or dimethyl adds extra carbons. Let's work them out simply.

$$\text{butan-1-ol} = 4 \text{ carbons} \rightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$$
$$\text{2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol} = 3 + 2 = 5 \text{ carbons} \rightarrow \text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$$

**Compare each pair**

Only one pair matches in total carbons. Butan-2-ol has 4 carbons, and 2-methylpropan-2-ol has 3 + 1 = 4 carbons.

$$\text{butan-2-ol} = \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$$
$$\text{2-methylpropan-2-ol} = \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$$
Same formula, different branching and position of OH, so they are isomers.

options.A: Incorrect. Butan-1-ol is C4H10O while 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol is C5H12O. Different molecular formulas, so they cannot be isomers.
options.B: Correct. Both have four carbons in total and formula C4H10O. Butan-2-ol is a straight chain secondary alcohol, while 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a branched tertiary alcohol, so they are structural isomers.
options.C: Incorrect. Pentan-1-ol is C5H12O while 2-methylpropan-2-ol is C4H10O. Students sometimes focus only on the -ol ending and forget to count total carbons including branches.
options.D: Incorrect. Propan-2-ol is C3H8O while 2-methylpropan-2-ol is C4H10O. They look similar because both are secondary or tertiary propan-2-ol types, but the extra methyl group changes the formula.
